column1: # The idea behind your book move, shown in the Openings tab. One line per move:
# side (b = Black, w = White), the moves from the start with your move last, then the idea.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5
column3: The point of 1...c6: d5 hits e4 with a pawn the c6 pawn already backs up, so you claim your share of the center right away.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5
column3: Same idea as against 2.d4: d5 challenges e4 at once, backed by the c6 pawn.

column2: e4 c6 Nc3 d5
column3: Same idea: d5 challenges e4 at once.

column2: e4 c6 Bc4 d5
column3: Hit the bishop and the e4 pawn together. If 3.exd5 cxd5, the bishop is attacked again and you keep a pawn on d5.

column2: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5
column3: Take back with the pawn: you keep a pawn in the center and the c4 bishop has to move again.

column2: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nf6
column3: Develop and add a defender to d5, which the b3 bishop is eyeing. Nc6 and e6 come next.

column2: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6
column3: Block the check with a developing move. The knight on c6 also eyes d4.

column2: e4 c6 f4 d5
column3: Same idea: d5 hits e4. White usually answers with e5, and then your bishop comes out to f5.

column2: e4 c6 f4 d5 e5 Bf5
column3: Get the light-squared bishop out before e6 shuts it in, the classic Caro-Kann idea.

column2: e4 c6 Qf3 d5
column3: Ignore the early queen and take the center. Your knight can come to f6 later and gain time against it.

column2: e4 c6 Qf3 d5 exd5 cxd5
column3: Take back with the pawn to keep a pawn on d5. Nf6 and Nc6 follow, often with tempo on the queen.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5
column3: Hit White's pawn chain at its base: c5 attacks d4 before White can support it with c3 and Nf3. Nc6 piles on next.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6
column3: Add a second attacker to d4. The plan is cxd4 and then Bg4, going after the knight that defends it.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4
column3: Trade on d4 first. After 6.cxd4 your bishop goes to g4 to pin the knight that holds d4.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4
column3: Pin the knight that defends d4. Then e6 and Nge7 to f5 add more pressure on d4.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 Nf3 Bg4
column3: Pin the knight that defends d4, so cxd4 and Nc6 win the fight for that pawn.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 Nc6
column3: Develop first. You can win the c5 pawn back later with e6 and Bxc5.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5
column3: Take back with the c-pawn so you keep a pawn on d5 and get the half-open c-file.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nc6
column3: Develop with pressure on d4. Nf6 and Bg4 come next.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4
column3: Take on e4. After 4.Nxe4 your bishop comes to f5 with tempo on the knight.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5
column3: Develop the bishop with tempo on the e4 knight, and get it outside your pawns before e6.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6
column3: Keep the bishop on its diagonal. If White pushes h4 and h5 later, h6 gives it a safe square on h7.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 h6
column3: Kick the knight right away. 6.Nxf7? just loses a piece: Kxf7 and your king is fine.

column2: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 h6 Nxf7 Kxf7
column3: Take the knight. White gave up a piece for one pawn, so get your king safe and develop.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5
column3: Take back with the c-pawn: you keep a pawn on d5 and get the half-open c-file.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5 d4 Nc6
column3: Develop with pressure on d4. Your light-squared bishop can still come to g4 or f5 before you play e6.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5 d4 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6
column3: Natural development: the knight covers d5 and e4. Bg4, pinning the f3 knight, comes next.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5 d4 Nc6 Bb5 a6
column3: Ask the bishop right away. If it takes on c6 you get the bishop pair, and if it drops back to a4, b5 gains space with tempo.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5 d4 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5
column3: Gain space with tempo on the bishop. After Bb3, your bishop comes to g4.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 exd5 cxd5 d4 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bb5 Bg4
column3: Pin the f3 knight. With your knight on c6 and bishop on g4, d4 is under pressure.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 e5 Bg4
column3: Get the bishop out before e6 shuts it in, and pin the f3 knight, which will defend d4.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 e5 Bg4 d4 e6
column3: Now e6 is fine because your bishop is already outside the pawn chain. c5 comes next to hit d4.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 e5 Bg4 d4 e6 Be2 c5
column3: Hit d4, the base of White's pawn chain. Nc6 adds more pressure.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 dxe4
column3: Take on e4. After 4.Nxe4 your bishop comes out to g4 with gain of time.

column2: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bg4
column3: Pin the f3 knight and get your bishop out before e6.

column2: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5
column3: Take back with the pawn so you keep a pawn in the center.

column2: d4 d5 c4
column3: The Queen's Gambit: c4 attacks d5 and offers a pawn to pull Black's center pawn away from the middle.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4
column3: Take the whole center while Black's pawn sits on c4. You win the pawn back later with Bxc4.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e6 Bxc4
column3: Win the pawn back. You keep the big center and develop easily with Nf3, Nc3 and O-O.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4
column3: Undermine the b5 pawn that protects c4. After c6, axb5 cxb5 and Nc3, the b5 pawn comes under fire.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e5 Nf3
column3: Develop with an attack on e5. After exd4, Bxc4 wins the pawn back with a lead in development.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e5 Nf3 exd4 Bxc4
column3: Win back the c4 pawn with a developing move. Castle next and use your lead in development.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 Nf6 e5
column3: Kick the knight with tempo and gain space. After Nd5, Bxc4 wins your pawn back.

column2: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 Nc6 Nf3
column3: Develop and protect d4. Bxc4 wins the pawn back later.

column2: d4 d5 c4 e6 cxd5
column3: Trade on d5 to fix Black's pawns early. Your pieces then aim at the d5 pawn.

column2: d4 d5 c4 e6 cxd5 exd5 Nf3
column3: Develop toward the center and keep an eye on e5. Your pieces go to their natural squares before you pick a plan.

column2: d4 d5 c4 e6 cxd5 exd5 Nf3 Nf6 g3
column3: Fianchetto the bishop so it presses on d5 from g2. Castle next.

column2: d4 d5 c4 e6 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3
column3: Develop with tempo on the queen.

column2: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5
column3: The Exchange Slav: a simple, symmetrical structure. Develop quickly and use the open c-file.

column2: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3
column3: Develop toward d5. In this quiet structure, smooth development counts most.

column2: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3
column3: Develop and control e5. Your dark-squared bishop comes out next, to f4 or g5.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5
column3: Against the Marshall Defense, take on d5. If the knight takes back, e4 kicks it with tempo.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Nxd5 e4
column3: Kick the knight with tempo and take the whole center.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nf6 Nc3
column3: Develop and defend e4. Your big pawn center is the edge.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nb6 Nf3
column3: Develop. Your d4 and e4 pawns give you the center, and Nc3, Be2 and O-O follow.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3
column3: Develop with tempo on the queen.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 cxd5
column3: Against the Chigorin, take on d5. Your d4 pawn becomes the target, so keep it covered.

column2: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 cxd5 Qxd5 Nf3
column3: Defend d4 with the knight. Not Nc3?: then Qxd4 wins a pawn, because only your queen guards d4.

column2: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5
column3: Take the pawn. After d4, develop with Nf3 and don't play e3: Bb4+ and dxe3 is a known trap (the Lasker Trap).

column2: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3
column3: Develop and keep the extra pawn. Avoid e3, which runs into Bb4+ and dxe3.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4
column3: Take space on the queenside and keep e4 in reserve. Most Indian defenses start here.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3
column3: Develop and support e4. If Bb4 (the Nimzo-Indian), your book answer is Bd2.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2
column3: Break the pin calmly. If Black takes on c3, take back with the bishop and keep your pawns healthy.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3
column3: Develop and get ready for e4, taking the full center against the King's Indian.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4
column3: Take the full center while Black's pieces are on the kingside.

column2: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3
column3: Develop. Be2 and O-O come next, the calm main line against the King's Indian.

column2: d4 e6 c4
column3: Take space. If d5 comes, it's a Queen's Gambit Declined. Against Bb4+ your book plays Nc3.

column2: d4 e5 dxe5
column3: Take the pawn: the Englund Gambit gives it up for very little. Just watch for the queen tricks on e7 and b4.

column2: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3
column3: Defend the e5 pawn with a developing move.

column2: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4
column3: Defend e5 with the bishop. Know the follow-up: Qb4+ Bd2, and after Qxb2 play Nc3.

column2: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2
column3: Block the check with the bishop. If Qxb2, Nc3 is the answer.

column2: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Nc3
column3: The famous trap is 6.Bc3? Bb4! and Black mates on c1. Nc3 shuts that down, and your pieces develop with tempo on the queen.

column2: d4 g6 c4
column3: Take space. You can add Nc3 and e4 next.

column2: d4 g6 c4 Bg7 Nf3
column3: Develop and control e5 and d4. Nc3 and e4 can follow.

column2: d4 c6 c4
column3: Take space with c4. After d5 it's a Slav.

column2: d4 d6 c4
column3: Take space. Nc3 and e4 can follow.

column2: d4 c5 d5
column3: Push past the c5 pawn and take space. Black's pieces get cramped behind it.

column2: d4 b6 e4
column3: Take the full center. Black's bishop on b7 will hit e4, so be ready to defend it with Nc3 or Bd3.
